posts.title: How to Layer Textures in a Modern Living Room
posts.excerpt: Linen, velvet, brass and wood — the combinations that add depth without clutter.
content: Texture is one of the fastest ways to make a room feel considered. When every surface shares the same finish, spaces can read flat — even when the furniture is beautiful.
Start with a foundation of natural materials: a wool rug, oak side table, or linen curtains. These set a calm base that more expressive pieces can sit on top of.
Introduce contrast with one statement texture — velvet on a sofa, a ceramic lamp base, or brushed brass hardware. The goal is balance, not competition.
Repeat a accent material in two places so the room feels intentional. If you use brass in a pendant, echo it in a mirror frame or tray.
Finish with soft layers: cushions, throws, and books. These are the details guests notice subconsciously — the room feels warm because it is layered, not because it is busy.

comments.text: Loved the tip about repeating brass twice — tried it and it really works.
Would love a follow-up on small apartments with the same approach.

posts.title: A Practical Guide to Sustainable Materials at Home
posts.excerpt: From FSC-certified wood to responsibly sourced linen — what to look for when you shop.
content: Sustainable design is not a single material choice — it is a series of thoughtful decisions about longevity, sourcing, and how a piece will live in your home for years.
Wood furniture should carry credible certification where possible. Kiln-dried hardwood frames and repairable construction extend the life of seating and tables.
Textiles matter too. Linen and organic cotton age gracefully, while performance fabrics can reduce the need for frequent replacement in high-traffic rooms.
Consider end-of-life: modular pieces, removable covers, and classic silhouettes stay relevant longer than trend-driven shapes.
The most sustainable item is often the one you keep. Invest in versatile staples and layer personality with smaller, replaceable accents.

comments.text: Clear and helpful — especially the note on repairable construction.

posts.title: Small-Space Styling: Five Rules That Actually Work
posts.excerpt: Make compact rooms feel open, intentional, and far from cramped.
content: Small rooms reward editing. Choose fewer, better pieces with clear purpose rather than filling every corner.
Use vertical lines — tall shelving, floor lamps, and hung curtains close to the ceiling — to draw the eye upward.
Mirrors and light tones expand perception, but contrast is still important. One darker accent anchors the room.
Multi-functional furniture — storage ottomans, extendable tables — reduces visual noise.
Leave breathing room at entry sightlines. The first view into a space sets the tone for how large it feels.

comments.text: The vertical lines tip changed our studio completely. Thank you!

posts.title: Seasonal Table Settings for Everyday Meals
posts.excerpt: Elevate weeknight dinners with linen, ceramics, and effortless centrepieces.
content: A beautiful table does not require a special occasion. Start with a neutral base — stoneware, clear glass, natural linen — and add one seasonal element.
In spring, fresh greenery or soft pastel napkins feel right. In autumn, warm wood boards and taper candles create atmosphere quickly.
Keep height low so conversation stays easy. Bud vases beat towering arrangements for daily use.
Mix matte and glossy finishes for subtle depth: a glazed bowl on a linen runner, matte plates with polished cutlery.

posts.title: Caring for Velvet Upholstery Year-Round
posts.excerpt: Simple habits to preserve colour, pile, and shape on velvet sofas and chairs.
content: Velvet develops character with use — light marking on the pile is normal and often settles with gentle brushing.
Vacuum weekly with an upholstery attachment. Work in the direction of the nap to lift fibres evenly.
Rotate cushions monthly so wear distributes naturally across the seat.
Keep velvet away from prolonged direct sunlight to preserve depth of colour.
For spills, blot immediately and avoid rubbing. Professional cleaning once a year keeps performance fabrics at their best.

comments.text: Didn't know about brushing direction — pile looks much better now.

posts.title: The Colour Palettes Shaping Interiors in 2026
posts.excerpt: Warm neutrals, muted greens, and grounded terracotta — how to use them at home.
content: This year favours warmth over stark minimalism. Cream, oat, and caramel create rooms that feel lived-in from day one.
Muted sage and olive pair beautifully with walnut and brass — a combination that works in both city flats and country homes.
Terracotta accents add energy without overpowering. Use them in ceramics, artwork, or a single accent chair.
When testing colour, view swatches at different times of day. North-facing rooms need warmer bases; bright spaces can handle cooler grey-greens.
Build palettes in ratios: 70% neutral foundation, 20% secondary tone, 10% accent.

comments.text: The 70/20/10 ratio made choosing paint so much easier.

posts.title: Designing a Calm Bedroom Retreat
posts.excerpt: Soft lighting, layered linen, and the furniture layout that supports better rest.
content: Bedrooms should signal rest the moment you enter. Start by reducing visual clutter — closed storage and a limited palette help.
Layer lighting at three heights: ambient ceiling or wall wash, bedside task lights, and a low accent for evening.
Choose breathable textiles. Linen and cotton regulate temperature and improve comfort through the seasons.
Position the bed to avoid direct alignment with harsh morning light if you are sensitive to early sun.
A single sculptural object on a bedside table — a ceramic vase, a small stack of books — is enough decoration.

posts.title: Outdoor Living: Extending Your Home Into the Garden
posts.excerpt: Furniture layouts, weather-ready textiles, and lighting for evenings outside.
content: Treat outdoor space as a room without walls. Define zones with rugs, planters, and furniture groupings.
Choose materials rated for your climate — teak and powder-coated aluminium perform well in variable weather.
Outdoor lighting should be low and warm. String lights, lanterns, and uplighting create ambience without glare.
Keep textiles weather-resistant or store cushions in a bench box when not in use.
A small bistro set can host morning coffee; a sectional arrangement suits weekend entertaining — plan for your real routines.

comments.text: Zone tip with planters worked brilliantly on our patio.
